title: Tangzhong Grain & Seed Bread
description: A soft, generous loaf with the soul of old-world baking — built on modern tangzhong and a hearty, soaked grain-and-seed mix that gives depth without stealing moisture.

ingredients.notes: divided: 30g for Tangzhong, 560g for Main Dough
divided: 190g for Tangzhong, 180g for Main Dough

method.instruction: Make the tangzhong: in a small saucepan, combine 30 g of the bread flour and 190 g of the water. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until it thickens into a paste at approximately 65°C. Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature.
Prepare the seed and grain mix: combine all seeds, grains, and add-ins in a bowl. Cover with hot water and let soak for 20–30 minutes. Drain thoroughly and squeeze out excess moisture.
In a large bowl, combine the remaining 560 g of bread flour, salt, sugar, yeast, and bread improver.
Add the cooled tangzhong, the remaining 180 g of water, vegetable oil, and the drained seed mixture.
Mix until a rough dough forms. The dough will feel firm initially — this is normal.
Knead for 12–15 minutes by hand or 8–10 minutes in a stand mixer until the dough becomes smooth and elastic. It will relax and become more pliable as you knead.
Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp tea towel, and let rise in a warm place for 1½–2 hours until doubled in size. The seeds make this dough denser, so it may rise more slowly.
Punch down the dough and shape into a loaf. Place in a greased loaf tin approximately 20–22 cm × 10–12 cm.
Cover and let rise for another 60–90 minutes until the dough has risen about 2 cm above the rim of the tin.
Optional: brush the top with water or milk and sprinkle with extra oats, sesame seeds, or sunflower seeds.
Bake for 32–38 minutes until the top is deep golden brown and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.
Remove from tin immediately and cool on a wire rack for at least 45 minutes before slicing.

notes.title: Why Soaking Matters
notes.content: The grain-and-seed mix is soaked because oats, bran, bulgur, freekeh, flax, chia, psyllium, and hemp absorb moisture. Soaking ensures the dough stays hydrated and the loaf rises tall with a tender crumb.

notes.title: Tangzhong + Seeds
notes.content: The tangzhong keeps the loaf soft for days, while the soaked seeds add hearty flavour and nutrition without weighing it down or stealing moisture from the dough.

notes.title: Customise Your Mix
notes.content: Do not worry if you are missing some seeds — use what you have. The total seed and grain weight should be around 145–150 g. Popular combinations include oats, sunflower, pumpkin, flax, and chia.
